Seroczyn Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Seroczyn, Poland

Demolished. Jews are recorded in Seroczyn as early as 1704; settlement developed further from the late 18th century, and by 1921, 179 Jews lived there, most murdered at Treblinka in 1942. The cemetery, likely established in the first half of the 19th century, is documented through a recorded kehilla in 1820 and burial-fee income from 1830. Germans used tombstones to reinforce roads during WWII, and local residents participated in further destruction. Poland formally closed the cemetery in 1963, with documentation noting the last burial occurred in 1943. Restoration began in 2011, when local workers recovered over 20 matzevot; a local club led cleanup in 2012, and the site was fenced by the ESJF in 2022.
